posts.hook: Planning season isn't about picking tactics. It's about deciding what you actually believe your organization can do.
posts.direction: Angle: most orgs open a blank planning doc and immediately jump to channels and budgets — skipping the conviction layer that makes any plan hold. Cover: why strategy without belief collapses under pressure; why mission-driven orgs have an advantage here if they use it. Graphic: quote card — pull the core conviction as a bold centered statement.

posts.hook: 3 questions to answer before you write a single word of your 2027 marketing plan.
posts.direction: Angle: most plans start with tactics; these three questions force clarity on audience, message, and goal first. Cover: Who are we actually trying to reach? What one thing do we want them to do? What does success look like in plain language? Frame as pre-work, not extra work. Graphic: tip card with a numbered list — one question per row, brief annotation under each.

posts.hook: If you want 2027 to feel different, the work starts before the calendar flips. We can help you build the plan.
posts.direction: Angle: soft close on the planning-season theme — not pressure, but an honest invitation. Cover: name the specific help offered (clarity on message, channel selection, a plan that fits the org's actual capacity). End with a low-friction CTA — DM or link to a discovery call. Graphic: quote card with the hook as the hero line and a one-line CTA beneath.
